comparison: Both evaluate C1-C5 (molecular characterization of Hif-3α isoforms) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the experimental evidence (RT-PCR, RACE, domain analysis). Peer review notes initial concerns about clarity of molecular differences and alternative start codon explanation, but these were addressed in revision and the claims were ultimately accepted.

Both address C6-C8 (expression patterns). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by qRT-PCR data. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, noting a discrepancy between qRT-PCR (Figure 1C-D) and RT-PCR amplicons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), specifically difficulty detecting amplicon in adult kidney despite high qRT-PCR levels. This discrepancy was not fully resolved.

Both evaluate oxygen-insensitivity claims (C9-C17, with peer review covering C9-C12, C14-C17) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights multiple experimental systems and mechanistic explanation via lack of ODD domain. Peer review indicates no concerns were raised about oxygen-insensitivity data, which was central to the manuscript's novelty and accepted by reviewers.

Both address transcriptional activity claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers C18-C27 (luciferase assays, HRE-dependence, domain analysis). Peer review covers broader set C18-C35 (including target gene specificity). Both note well-controlled experiments; peer review indicates concerns focused on in vivo phenotypes rather than basic transcriptional characterization.

OpenEval evaluates C28-C35 (target gene activation in zebrafish) as SUPPORTED with qRT-PCR data and appropriate controls. Peer review R4 covers overlapping claims C28-C35 within broader transcriptional characterization (C18-C35), also marking as SUPPORTED with no specific concerns about target gene specificity.

Both address growth effects (C36-C38). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes mechanism not elucidated. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN with major concerns about general growth retardation, developmental delays, and unhealthy-looking embryos suggesting overexpression artifacts. Peer review emphasizes need for tissue-specific manipulation and more rigorous validation.

Both evaluate LR asymmetry phenotypes. OpenEval covers C39-C48 as SUPPORTED, emphasizing specificity to Hif-3α2 and novel findings. Peer review (R5) covers overlapping claims C39-C42, C44-C48 as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about overexpression artifacts and sensitivity of KV-dependent laterality processes. Initial concerns were significant though manuscript was deemed improved after revision.

Both address KV/DFC phenotypes (C49-C55, with overlap on C51-C55). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though notes direct causality not proven. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, noting non-significant trends in sox17 and DFC numbers, and requesting detailed KV morphology/cilia analysis. Round 2 reviewers still asked about DFC cluster size determination methodology.

Both evaluate C56-C70 (Wnt signaling inhibition) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes pathway specificity and placement downstream of GSK3β. Peer review initially expressed concerns about specificity in context of general developmental defects, but revised manuscript with additional controls appears to have addressed concerns, with manuscript deemed substantially improved.

Both evaluate C71-C76 (CRISPR mutant generation and characterization) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes sophisticated genetic tool and preservation of Hif-3α1 function. Peer review initially raised major concerns about unclear molecular characterization and need to demonstrate Hif-3α1 is unaffected, but revised manuscript adequately addressed these with only nomenclature changes requested in Round 2.

Both evaluate C77-C80 (mutant Wnt signaling phenotypes) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes genetic loss-of-function complements gain-of-function studies. Peer review initially questioned whether qPCR changes resulted from general defects, but second allele and chemical sensitization experiments (Lithium, BIO) satisfied concerns about specificity.

Both address C81-C89 (mutant mortality and developmental phenotypes). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting variability and surprising lack of major patterning defects. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, questioning why high mortality occurs without expected morphological changes and whether Wnt effects are relatively minor. The discrepancy between mortality and morphology in survivors remains somewhat puzzling.

Both evaluate C90-C96 (morpholino phenotypes) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes MO specificity controls and suggests compensatory mechanisms in mutants versus morphants. Peer review acknowledges general skepticism about morpholino data but indicates appropriate controls (p53, genetic rescue) satisfied concerns, with MO data complementing genetic analysis.

Both evaluate C97-C103 (temporal dynamics and compensation) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes temporal distinction between mutants and morphants supporting compensation hypothesis. Peer review indicates temporal analysis and chemical sensitization address requests for genetic interactions, with compensatory mechanism providing reasonable explanation for mutant-morphant discrepancy.

Both evaluate C104-C108 (human cell conservation) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes evolutionary conservation and translational relevance. Peer review indicates no concerns were raised about human cell data or pathway specificity, with experiments strengthening manuscript by demonstrating conservation.

Both address C110-C123 (β-catenin interaction and degradation). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, emphasizing novel nuclear degradation mechanism. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, noting modest direct interaction in GST pull-down and questioning whether other factors are involved or post-translational modifications needed. Also questions interpretation of MG132/LEF1 data. Concerns may not have been fully resolved.

Both evaluate C124-C137 (structure-function analysis separating transcriptional and degradation activities) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive mutant analysis and in vivo validation. Peer review initially noted interpretation inconsistency regarding M2 mutant but overall structure-function analysis appears sound, with separation of activities well-demonstrated and in vivo validation strengthening conclusions.
